Objective / Description: Verify that with PCLK tied to HCLK in a single clock domain, the bridge initializes to the documented clean idle reset state.
Verify that PCLK is edge-aligned to HCLK throughout bringup so no clock-domain-crossing behavior is exercised.
Verify the bridge in single-clock-domain config returns to idle on reset and accepts a new transfer immediately afterward.
Verify that bringup operates under one clock domain only and no CDC handling (synchronizers, async resets) is exercised.
Verify the HADDR address bus is fully connected by driving minimum and maximum address values and confirming the bridge captures and translates them onto PADDR.
Verify the HWDATA write data bus is fully connected by driving walking/boundary patterns and confirming they appear on PWDATA.
Verify a write followed by a read returns matching data through HRDATA, confirming read-data bus connectivity and write/read correspondence.
Verify HCLK is connected and that all state progression and signal captures occur synchronously on HCLK rising edges.
Verify HRESETn is connected by asserting reset and confirming all source-side and peripheral-side outputs assume their documented reset values.
Verify PADDR drives both minimum and maximum address values correctly through the peripheral-side interface.
Verify PWDATA correctly carries walking/boundary data patterns from source to peripheral side.
Verify peripheral read data on PRDATA is correctly returned and read-back matches the value placed on PRDATA.
Verify peripheral-side phase progression (SETUP->ACTIVE) advances only on PCLK rising edges.
Verify PRESETn forces peripheral outputs to their defined reset values and the interface recovers after deassertion.
Verify that asserting SOFT_RST while a transfer is active clears active transfer state and returns the model to a clean idle state.
Verify SOFT_RST clears sticky STATUS error flags that were set by error scenarios.
Verify SOFT_RST preserves configuration bits (TIMEOUT_VAL, TIMEOUT_EN, ENABLE) while clearing transient/sticky state.
Verify the distinction between SOFT_RST behavior (preserves config) and full HRESETn hard reset (restores all defaults including CTRL).
Verify that asserting hard reset while the bridge is idle returns all outputs and registers to their documented reset values.
Verify that asserting hard reset while a transfer is in the ACTIVE/WAITING phase aborts the transfer cleanly and restores all reset values.
Verify that hard reset clears sticky STATUS error bits (ERR_INT, TIMEOUT_ERR, PSLVERR, ADDR_ERR) and captured debug registers ERROR_ADDR/ERROR_INFO.
Verify the bridge is immediately ready to accept and complete a new transfer on the first cycle after reset release, with all registers at reset values.
Verify STATUS register reflects its specified reset state with READY asserted and no sticky errors set.
Verify PSLVERR and aggregated ERR_INT sticky bits in STATUS are set and preserved after a target error event.
Verify Write-1-to-Clear behavior: a 1 in the written bit clears the corresponding sticky flag while 0 leaves others untouched.
Verify BUSY/READY reflect live model state and are immune to software writes.
Verify the CTRL register powers up to its specified reset value with ENABLE set and TIMEOUT_VAL=3'b111.
Verify R/W fields in CTRL accept programmed values and read back correctly.
Verify SOFT_RST bit write triggers a soft reset that clears sticky STATUS flags and preserves CTRL config bits.
Verify CTRL reserved bits remain 0 and are not affected by attempted writes of all-ones.
Verify ERROR_ADDR captures the source-side address of an address-error transaction.
Verify ERROR_INFO captures direction/beat/error-class context for a target-side (PSLVERR) error.
Verify both captured debug registers clear to 0x0000_0000 on hard reset.
Verify attempted APB writes to ERROR_ADDR/ERROR_INFO have no effect on stored value.
Verify a subsequent error overwrites the previously captured ERROR_ADDR.
Verify CTRL reset value and read/write behavior of writable bits via the peripheral-side register access path.
Verify STATUS reset value and write-1-to-clear semantics on sticky error bits while RO bits are unaffected.
Verify RO debug registers reset to 0, capture error context on an error event, and reject write attempts.
Verify each defined offset decodes to the correct register and that the 4-byte stride mapping is correct.
Verify a single (non-sequence) HTRANS=NONSEQ write transfer with HSIZE=word advances address correctly and completes as one target access (sequence baseline).
Verify an incrementing multi-transfer sequence (NONSEQ then SEQ) with HSIZE=word produces target addresses advancing by 0x4 per beat, handled in-order.
Verify HSIZE-dependent address stride: a SEQ sequence with HSIZE=halfword advances target PADDR by 0x2 per beat, distinct from the word case.
Verify multi-transfer sequence data integrity by writing distinct patterns (all 1s, all 0s, alternating) then reading back and comparing, confirming in-order handling.
Verify a single source-side write (HADDR/HWDATA) is correctly captured and translated to a target-side write access (PADDR/PWDATA) following the capture->setup->active->complete sequence.
Verify a source-side read translates to a target-side read access and that HRDATA reflects PRDATA only after target completion.
Verify data integrity across translation for all-ones, all-zeros, and alternating bit patterns on 32-bit HWDATA/PWDATA.
Verify address translation integrity at low, mid, and high 32-bit address boundaries.
Verify the strict two-phase target-side progression (setup then active) and that PENABLE is never asserted in the same cycle as the initial PSEL assertion.
Verify that a single PREADY=0 wait state holds the APB transfer in the ACTIVE phase and delays HREADY_OUT to the source side.
Verify that during a multi-cycle PREADY=0 stall on a read, HREADY_OUT stays low and HRDATA is presented only at the cycle PREADY=1.
Verify data integrity (all 1s, all 0s, alternating) survives PREADY back-pressure on consecutive writes and PWDATA is held stable during each stall.
Verify that persistent PREADY=0 with timeout enabled eventually terminates the held transfer and sets STATUS.TIMEOUT_ERR, while HREADY_OUT remains low until the timeout fires.
Verify a single read transfer returns PRDATA on HRDATA only after the target-side active phase completes (PREADY=1).
Verify HRDATA is NOT returned and source completion is gated while target is stalled (PREADY=0), then returns correct data once PREADY asserts.
Verify the read-data return path preserves data integrity for all-1s, all-0s, and alternating bit patterns from PRDATA to HRDATA.
Verify read data returned on HRDATA correlates with the correct target address across the 32-bit address range (low, mid, high).
Verify that when target signals PSLVERR=1, HRESP=1 (error) is returned and the read-data return path reflects the error rather than valid data delivery.
Verify that an accepted source-side request is captured and translated into a target-side SETUP phase with correct PSEL/PENABLE signaling and timing.
Verify the target active phase completes correctly when PREADY asserts and source-side completion (HREADY_OUT) is then released.
Verify that during a target stall the ACTIVE phase signals remain stable and HREADY_OUT stays low until PREADY asserts.
Verify on a read transfer that HRDATA is not presented to the source until target completion (PREADY=1) occurs in the active phase.
Verify that a single target stall (PREADY=0) holds PENABLE asserted and delays HREADY_OUT until PREADY=1.
Verify PSEL, PENABLE, PADDR remain stable and HREADY_OUT remains deasserted across several consecutive PREADY=0 wait cycles.
Verify that HRDATA is not presented as valid until PREADY=1 completes the target access, and HREADY_OUT gating matches.
Verify the bridge correctly releases back-pressure after a stalled transfer and accepts a new transfer with proper PSEL/PENABLE sequencing.
Verify the IDLE-to-SETUP transition asserts PSEL with PENABLE deasserted on the first target-side cycle.
Verify the SETUP-to-ACTIVE transition asserts PENABLE while keeping PSEL high.
Verify ACTIVE self-loop on PREADY=0 and stability of PSEL/PENABLE during wait states.
Verify handshake completion (PREADY=1) returns FSM to IDLE and deasserts PSEL/PENABLE.
Verify the complete state-machine sequence with correct PSEL/PENABLE/PREADY timing across all phases.
Verify HRESP=0 (OK) is asserted on the source side at completion of a normal write transfer with no target error.
Verify HRESP=1 (error) is driven on the source side when PSLVERR=1 is asserted during the target active phase.
Verify HRESP=1 (error) on the source side when a target timeout occurs (PREADY never asserted within window).
Verify HRESP remains 0 (no premature/spurious error) throughout target wait states and resolves to OK at completion when PREADY finally asserts without error.
Verify that a request to an invalid address range sets ADDR_ERR, returns HRESP error, captures ERROR_ADDR, and that the model recovers cleanly and shows a clean error log after recovery.
Verify that the first address immediately above the highest valid range triggers ADDR_ERR while the last valid address does not, and that ERROR_ADDR captures the exact boundary-violating address.
Verify that an invalid-address READ transaction is detected, ERROR_ADDR captures the read address, ERROR_INFO captures read direction, and HRDATA is not treated as valid data.
Verify address error detection on a request following a valid in-flight transfer, then verify hard/soft reset cleanly aborts and clears sticky ADDR_ERR and captured debug registers.
Verify a timeout error is detected, captured in STATUS, and logged when PREADY is never asserted within the programmed window.
Verify that with TIMEOUT_EN=0 a prolonged PREADY=0 stall does not set TIMEOUT_ERR or HRESP, but instead holds completion (negative/control test).
Verify timeout error sets both TIMEOUT_ERR and aggregated ERR_INT when interrupt indication is enabled, captures debug context, and both clear via W1C.
Verify the timeout window boundary: just-in-time PREADY completes without error, while one-cycle-late PREADY triggers TIMEOUT_ERR.

Verify a single target-side error (PSLVERR=1) during an active access is detected, propagated to HRESP, captured in ERROR_INFO/STATUS, and the model recovers cleanly with clean error log after recovery.
Verify target error injected on a read transfer is captured with read direction in ERROR_INFO, HRDATA is not treated as valid completion, and recovery restores clean operation.
Verify the sticky behavior of STATUS.PSLVERR after a target error — flag persists across subsequent good (non-error) traffic and is only removed by W1C/soft reset.

Verify target error injected on a specific beat of an ordered multi-transfer sequence is captured with beat index/context in ERROR_INFO and that error capture does not corrupt earlier completed beats.
Verify a target error (PSLVERR) during the active phase produces HRESP=1 on the source side within the error response window, and the error is logged and recoverable.
Verify the precise cycle timing of HRESP assertion relative to PSLVERR sampling and the error response window before HREADY_OUT completes.
Verify the address-error class generates HRESP=1, sets ADDR_ERR sticky, captures the offending address, and is recoverable, distinct from a target PSLVERR path.
Verify a target error transfer immediately followed (after clear) by a normal transfer does not produce a stale HRESP or stale sticky bits, proving error response window isolation.
